headline: Prey animals have evolved survival strategies—speed, vigilance, numbers, and deception keep them alive
universal_truth: Vulnerability drives innovation; those under pressure develop the most creative solutions
fun_facts: A rabbit's eyes are positioned to see nearly 360 degrees without moving its head
Zebra stripes may confuse predators by making it hard to single out one animal from the herd
Some prey animals can literally die of fright—sudden cardiac arrest from extreme stress
discussion_questions: What survival strategies have you developed?
How has vulnerability made you more resourceful?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: Predators are impressive, but prey animals are equally remarkable. Rabbits with panoramic vision. Gazelles that outrun cheetahs. Fish that school in confusing patterns. Being hunted is a powerful evolutionary pressure—it produces creative survival solutions.

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: Prey are under constant threat, yet they persist. Their survival strategies are diverse and ingenious. What does being prey teach about survival?

options.text: Vulnerability drives innovation—being hunted forces development of detection, evasion, deception, and cooperation strategies that wouldn't emerge without pressure
options.response: Yes. Predation pressure created 360-degree vision, explosive speed, herding behavior, and camouflage. Threat drives adaptation. Vulnerability can be a source of strength.

options.text: Prey just run away or hide
options.response: Running and hiding are strategies, but the sophistication is remarkable...

q1.title: Detection
q1.script: Many prey evolved hyper-awareness: eyes that see everywhere, ears that hear everything, instincts that trigger at the slightest signal. Early warning is often the difference between escape and capture.

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: Speed and Evasion
q2.script: Some prey simply outrun predators. Gazelles can maintain speeds that exhaust cheetahs. Rabbits zigzag unpredictably. Speed and evasive action create survival through escape.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: Safety in Numbers
q3.script: Herds and schools protect individuals. Predators struggle to single out targets from crowds. Many eyes spot threats faster. Collective defense works—there's genuine safety in numbers.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Vulnerability drives innovation. Those under pressure develop the most creative solutions. Your challenges may be forging your greatest strengths.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 249. Tomorrow, we'll explore hiding in plain sight—camouflage. Until then, consider what survival strategies pressure has developed in you.
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Survival Strategy - What Has Pressure Taught You?
growTrack.activity: What threats or pressures have you faced? What survival strategies did you develop in response—detection, evasion, cooperation? Often our greatest capabilities came from our greatest challenges. Vulnerability forges strength.
